subject: Food Science
title: Osmosis in Cooking
description: A quick win: understand Osmosis in Cooking.

hook.text: Sprinkle salt on a cucumber slice and water pours out. Osmosis moves water from low-salt to high-salt areas.

buildup.text: Cell membranes are semi-permeable—water passes through, but dissolved salts and sugars can't.

discovery.text: Brining a turkey works by osmosis in reverse—salt enters cells, pulling water with it, making meat juicier.

twist.text: Sugar does the same thing. Strawberries macerated in sugar release juice as water moves out by osmosis.

climax.text: Osmosis is why salt-preserved fish and sugar-preserved jam resist spoilage—water leaves the microbes too.

punchline.text: Water follows the salt. Understanding osmosis makes you a better cook.

quiz.question: How does brining make meat juicier?
options: It adds water to the surface
Salt enters cells and pulls water in through osmosis
Heat from brine cooks the meat
